openings.delta: Add record-to-claim dependencies to the indexed alias ledger. Input is newly absent manifest identifiers after removal; path is an identifier-set difference followed by dependency lookup. Response retracts affected claims, checks surviving dictionary-authorized boundary aliases, and recomputes supported stages or intervals. Removed-record contents cannot support final claims.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: G0444:R1 reruns the whole alias review. Targeted revalidation may require fewer manual inspections while producing equally supported frozen reports. A removed sole carrier should widen its interval; a surviving authorized alias may cancel that response. Preexisting absences, identifier ambiguity, and unrelated deletions can falsely signal relevance. These are predictions, not supplied results.
openings.probe: On each disjoint three-pair subset, derive both variants from identical supplied records. Record baseline identifiers and claim dependencies, then apply the stipulated removals during final review. Compare affected-claim queues, actual retractions, surviving citations, interval changes and total manual inspections, counting repeats across both variants against twelve per pair. Freeze all six reports before opening either sealed sheet; compare boundaries only where sheets provide answers. Complete analysis within sixty minutes and comparison within twenty additional minutes. If removal affects no claim, record a null signal without inventing an informative contrast.
assumptions: Identifiers permit detecting newly absent records; dependency tracking includes earlier-boundary evidence and alias authorization.
Dictionary identity and surviving digests may be unavailable; then keep the interval unresolved.
Implementation and review fit the time and shared inspection capacity; answer-sheet coverage remains unspecified.

assessment: Defeat: incomplete dependency tracking, stale citations, unsupported alias identity, insufficient preceding evidence, or exceeded capacity. Missing records and blank warnings prove neither nonexecution nor absence of problems. Preserve manifest ordering as indexing; separate observed mismatches from explanations. Definite earliest-stage claims require supplied surviving records excluding earlier boundaries; otherwise report a referenced interval and feasible adjacent-record next check. This is a probe, not deployment.
